newsitem.title: UK: SW Water aims for 8 pct real div increases.
newsitem.headline: SW Water aims for 8 pct real div increases.

text.p: British water and sewerage company South West Water said on Thursday it intended to pay out a final dividend for the year up around 20 percent from the previous year and then look for eight percent real annual increases.
"The dividend policy will continue to be based on the pursuit of progressive growth," the company said in a statement with first half results.
South West Water paid out an interim dividend of 11.8 pence per share, up from 9.8 pence previously and saw pretax profits rise to 72.9 million stg from 54.0 million stg a year ago.

The company added that it would exercise its power to buy back up to 10 percent of shares, agreed at the annual meeting in July, "only...if it believes it is in the best interests of the company's shareholders."
South West Water promised the interim dividend increase after two proposed bids for it, from Severn Trent and Wessex were blocked by the UK government in October as against the public interest.
It also said it would pay a rebate to customers of 15 stg by June 1997 and provision for the cost would be made in the second half of the year.
The company said that in the first half, an additional leasing facility provided 5.7 million stg profit and should contribute annual profit of nine million stg in each of the next three years.
The facility involves standby letters of credit which are counter-indemnified by cash deposits, the company said.
South West Water said it had cut leakage to 21 percent from 28 percent in 1992 and was "on track to meet our own target of 15 percent leakage...by the end of 1999."
It said capital expenditure was 61.6 million stg in the first half of the year and "a further substantial uplift is planned for the second half."
South West Water said Alan Fletcher, currently non-executive deputy chairman, would not take on the role of non-executive chairman when Keith Court, the current chairman, steps down in February 1997.
It said Stanislas Yassukovich would replace Fletcher and also be responsible for selection and appointment of a new group chief executive from outside the company. -- London Newsroom +44 171 5427717
